AZN.L.content: AstraZeneca on Tuesday said it had agreed to acquire US biotechnology company Fusion Therapeutics for $2.4 billion in cash, in its biggest oncology deal this year. The acquisition adds a late-stage radiopharmaceutical candidate for prostate cancer to AstraZeneca's pipeline, with peak sales potential estimated above $3 billion. Analysts said the deal multiple looked reasonable given the scarcity value of radiopharma assets.
AZN.L.snippet: AstraZeneca said it agreed to acquire US biotech Fusion Therapeutics for $2.4 billion in cash to strengthen its oncology pipeline.
AZN.L.title: AstraZeneca to acquire Fusion Therapeutics in $2.4bn oncology deal

AZN.L.content: AstraZeneca reported third-quarter core earnings per share 12% ahead of analyst consensus, driven by strong oncology and rare-disease sales. The drugmaker raised its full-year guidance, now expecting high-teens revenue growth and low-twenties core EPS growth. Management cited accelerating launches in the US and China.
AZN.L.snippet: AstraZeneca reported third-quarter core earnings 12% ahead of consensus and raised its full-year guidance for revenue and profit.
AZN.L.title: AstraZeneca Q3 earnings beat estimates by 12%, raises full-year guidance

AZN.L.content: The US Food and Drug Administration has granted priority review to AstraZeneca's experimental lung cancer therapy datopotamab, the company said. A regulatory decision is expected within six months, potentially opening a multi-billion-dollar indication. The drug showed strong progression-free survival data in a late-stage trial published last month.
AZN.L.snippet: The FDA granted priority review to AstraZeneca's experimental lung cancer therapy, with a decision expected within six months.
AZN.L.title: FDA grants priority review to AstraZeneca lung cancer drug

AZN.L.content: AstraZeneca's board declared an interim dividend of $1.03 per share, payable in December. The payout is consistent with the company's progressive dividend policy and was widely expected by analysts. No change to the full-year dividend outlook was announced.
AZN.L.snippet: AstraZeneca declared an interim dividend of $1.03 per share, in line with its progressive dividend policy.
AZN.L.title: AstraZeneca declares interim dividend of $1.03 per share

AZN.L.content: AstraZeneca chief executive said in an interview that pricing pressure and volume-based procurement in China remain headwinds for the industry. He reiterated, however, that the company's long-term growth outlook is intact, supported by the oncology portfolio. No new financial targets were disclosed.
AZN.L.snippet: AstraZeneca's CEO said pricing pressure in China remains a headwind but reiterated confidence in the long-term growth outlook.
AZN.L.title: AstraZeneca CEO says China headwinds persist but long-term outlook intact

AZN.L.content: Several brokers raised their price targets on AstraZeneca after the company's R&D day, citing underappreciated late-stage readouts. The average target now implies modest upside from current levels. Analysts cautioned that much of the good news is already reflected in the shares.
AZN.L.snippet: Brokers lifted their price targets on AstraZeneca following a well-received R&D pipeline update.
AZN.L.title: Analysts raise AstraZeneca price target after strong pipeline update

AZN.L.content: AstraZeneca has beaten quarterly forecasts and lifted its full-year expectations, sending shares higher in morning trading. Revenue grew strongly across its cancer medicines portfolio. The company said demand in emerging markets remained robust despite pricing pressures.
AZN.L.snippet: The pharmaceutical giant beat quarterly forecasts and increased its expectations for the full year.
AZN.L.title: AstraZeneca beats Q3 forecasts and lifts guidance

AZN.L.content: AstraZeneca has opened a new research and development facility in Cambridge, creating around 400 scientific jobs. The site will focus on early-stage discovery in oncology and immunology. The investment forms part of a previously announced UK expansion programme.
AZN.L.snippet: AstraZeneca opened a new research facility in Cambridge, creating 400 scientific jobs.
AZN.L.title: AstraZeneca opens new Cambridge R&D facility

AZN.L.content: AstraZeneca edged higher in morning trade as the FTSE 100 opened in positive territory. The shares added 0.6% in early dealing. Broader market sentiment was supported by overnight gains in Asia.
AZN.L.snippet: AstraZeneca was among the risers as the FTSE 100 opened higher on Tuesday.
AZN.L.title: FTSE 100 movers: AstraZeneca edges higher in morning trade

AZN.L.content: A generic version of one of AstraZeneca's established diabetes medicines received tentative approval in the United States, paving the way for cheaper competition next year. The drug generated around $800 million in US sales last year. Analysts said the impact is manageable but will weigh on the mature-products division.
AZN.L.snippet: A generic rival to one of AstraZeneca's diabetes medicines won tentative US approval, pressuring future sales.
AZN.L.title: AstraZeneca faces generic competition for key diabetes drug in US

HSBA.L.content: HSBC announced a $3 billion share buyback after third-quarter pre-tax profit came in ahead of analyst expectations. The lender credited resilient net interest income and lower-than-expected credit losses. The buyback will commence immediately and completes the capital return programme announced earlier this year.
HSBA.L.snippet: HSBC unveiled a $3 billion share buyback after third-quarter profit beat expectations.
HSBA.L.title: HSBC announces $3bn share buyback after Q3 profit beat

HSBA.L.content: HSBC's board has formally begun the search for a successor to its chief executive, who intends to step down in 2027 after a multi-year tenure. The bank said the process would consider internal and external candidates. Investors will watch closely for continuity in strategy, particularly around the Asia pivot.
HSBA.L.snippet: HSBC's board has begun searching for a successor to its chief executive, who plans to step down in 2027.
HSBA.L.title: HSBC board begins CEO succession search as chief plans 2027 exit

HSBA.L.content: HSBC raised its full-year guidance for net interest income, pointing to resilient deposit margins and hedging income. The upgrade implies low-single-digit upside to consensus earnings. Management cautioned that the benefit depends on the path of interest rates.
HSBA.L.snippet: HSBC raised its full-year net interest income guidance, citing resilient margins.
HSBA.L.title: HSBC raises guidance for net interest income

HSBA.L.content: Financial regulators have fined HSBC £85 million for failures in its transaction monitoring systems over a three-year period. The bank said it had invested heavily to remediate the issues and that no financial crime was found to have occurred. The fine was already provisioned, limiting the earnings impact.
HSBA.L.snippet: Regulators fined HSBC £85 million for failures in transaction monitoring systems.
HSBA.L.title: HSBC fined £85m by regulators over transaction monitoring failures

HSBA.L.content: HSBC declared a quarterly dividend of $0.10 per share, consistent with its payout policy. The dividend will be paid next month to shareholders on the register. Analysts noted the announcement contained no surprises.
HSBA.L.snippet: HSBC declared a quarterly dividend in line with its stated payout policy.
HSBA.L.title: HSBC declares quarterly dividend of $0.10 per share

HSBA.L.content: HSBC has completed the sale of its Canadian retail banking business, a further step in its strategic pivot toward Asia. Proceeds will support shareholder returns. The disposal removes a sub-scale operation that contributed modestly to group profit.
HSBA.L.snippet: HSBC completed the sale of its Canadian retail banking operations, sharpening its focus on Asia.
HSBA.L.title: HSBC completes sale of Canadian retail banking business

HSBA.L.content: HSBC said its Asian wealth business continued to grow strongly, with affluent client numbers climbing at a double-digit pace. The unit is central to the bank's strategy of capturing wealth flows in the region. Fee income from wealth management rose year on year.
HSBA.L.snippet: HSBC's Asian wealth business posted strong growth in client assets.
HSBA.L.title: Asia wealth unit drives HSBC growth as affluent client numbers climb

HSBA.L.content: HSBC shareholders have a busy week with the shares trading ex-dividend and sector-wide stress test chatter. The stock has tracked the wider banking sector in recent sessions. No company-specific announcements are scheduled.
HSBA.L.snippet: A look at the key dates and data points for HSBC shareholders this week.
HSBA.L.title: HSBC share price: what investors are watching this week

HSBA.L.content: HSBC has appointed a new chief risk officer, who will join next quarter from a rival bank. The appointment fills a vacancy left earlier this year. The bank said the new hire brings deep experience in credit and operational risk.
HSBA.L.snippet: HSBC named a new chief risk officer, effective next quarter.
HSBA.L.title: HSBC appoints new chief risk officer

HSBA.L.content: Proposals for a new levy on large UK banks to fund consumer protection measures could add hundreds of millions in annual costs across the sector. HSBC, as one of the largest lenders, would be among the contributors. The industry is lobbying for the plans to be scaled back.
HSBA.L.snippet: Proposals for a new levy on UK banks, including HSBC, could raise costs across the sector.
HSBA.L.title: UK banks face proposals for new levy to fund consumer protection

RR.L.content: Rolls-Royce has won a £9 billion contract to design and build nuclear propulsion systems for the UK's next-generation submarines. The multi-decade deal secures thousands of jobs in Derby. Analysts said the contract underpins long-term defence revenue visibility.
RR.L.snippet: Rolls-Royce secured a £9 billion contract to provide nuclear propulsion for the UK's submarine fleet.
RR.L.title: Rolls-Royce wins £9bn UK nuclear submarine propulsion contract

RR.L.content: Rolls-Royce raised its full-year underlying operating profit guidance after a strong first half driven by civil aerospace aftermarket growth. Large engine flying hours continued to recover. The company also upgraded its free cash flow outlook.
RR.L.snippet: Rolls-Royce raised its full-year profit guidance following a strong first half.
RR.L.title: Rolls-Royce raises profit guidance after strong first half

RR.L.content: Rolls-Royce's small modular reactor (SMR) design has been selected as the preferred technology for the Czech Republic's new nuclear programme. The deal could lead to multiple reactor orders worth billions. It marks the first major export win for the SMR business.
RR.L.snippet: Rolls-Royce's small modular reactor design was selected for the Czech Republic's nuclear programme.
RR.L.title: Rolls-Royce SMR selected for Czech nuclear programme

RR.L.content: Rolls-Royce reinstated its dividend for the first time in five years, declaring an interim payout. The move signals confidence in the balance sheet recovery. The board said future payouts would be progressive but prudent.
RR.L.snippet: Rolls-Royce reinstated its dividend for the first time in five years.
RR.L.title: Rolls-Royce reinstates dividend after five-year pause

RR.L.content: Rolls-Royce said large engine flying hours are approaching pre-pandemic levels, supporting its lucrative long-term service agreements. Widebody traffic recovery in Asia was the main driver. The company expects hours to exceed 2019 levels next year.
RR.L.snippet: Engine flying hours, key to Rolls-Royce's aftermarket revenue, are approaching pre-pandemic levels.
RR.L.title: Rolls-Royce engine flying hours near pre-pandemic levels

RR.L.content: Rolls-Royce shares touched a record high as investors continued to price in defence contract wins. The stock has more than doubled over the past year. Some analysts warn valuations now look stretched.
RR.L.snippet: Rolls-Royce shares touched a record high as defence optimism continued.
RR.L.title: Rolls-Royce shares hit record high on defence optimism

RR.L.content: Supply chain pressures are gradually easing for aircraft engine manufacturers, with lead times improving. Rolls-Royce and peers have struggled with parts shortages. Executives cautioned that skilled labour remains tight.
RR.L.snippet: Supply chain pressures are easing for aircraft engine manufacturers including Rolls-Royce.
RR.L.title: Supply chain pressures ease for aircraft engine makers

RR.L.content: Rolls-Royce has joined industry trials testing 100% sustainable aviation fuel on commercial aircraft engines. The tests aim to demonstrate compatibility without engine modifications. Commercial deployment timelines remain uncertain.
RR.L.snippet: Rolls-Royce joined trials of 100% sustainable aviation fuel on commercial engines.
RR.L.title: Rolls-Royce partners on sustainable aviation fuel trials

RR.L.content: Analysts are debating whether Rolls-Royce shares remain good value after more than doubling. Bulls cite the transformed balance sheet and defence pipeline; bears point to demanding multiples. The consensus remains cautiously positive.
RR.L.snippet: Analysts debate whether Rolls-Royce shares remain good value after a strong rally.
RR.L.title: Analyst Q&A: is Rolls-Royce still a buy after the rally?

RR.L.content: Rolls-Royce led the FTSE 100 risers in early trading, up 2.1%. The broader index was little changed. Traders cited continued momentum from recent contract news.
RR.L.snippet: Rolls-Royce led FTSE 100 risers in early trading.
RR.L.title: FTSE 100 movers: Rolls-Royce leads risers

SHEL.L.content: Shell has approved a $6 billion deepwater oil project in the Gulf of Mexico, its largest upstream sanction this year. The project is expected to produce 120,000 barrels per day at peak and deliver strong returns at current prices. First oil is targeted for late 2029.
SHEL.L.snippet: Shell gave the final investment decision for a $6 billion deepwater project in the Gulf of Mexico.
SHEL.L.title: Shell approves $6bn Gulf of Mexico deepwater oil project

SHEL.L.content: Shell reported third-quarter adjusted earnings below analyst expectations, hit by sharply weaker refining margins and lower gas trading results. Upstream production was steady. The company maintained its dividend and buyback pace, but analysts trimmed near-term forecasts.
SHEL.L.snippet: Shell's third-quarter earnings missed expectations as refining margins weakened sharply.
SHEL.L.title: Shell Q3 earnings miss on weaker refining margins

SHEL.L.content: Shell raised its quarterly dividend by 4% and extended its $3.5 billion share buyback programme into next quarter. The moves underscore the balance sheet strength despite the earnings miss. Total shareholder distributions this year are on track for record levels.
SHEL.L.snippet: Shell raised its quarterly dividend and extended its share buyback programme.
SHEL.L.title: Shell raises dividend and extends $3.5bn buyback programme

SHEL.L.content: A court has ordered Shell to deepen its planned emissions cuts, ruling that its current targets are insufficient. The company said it would appeal, arguing the decision oversteps into corporate strategy. Legal experts said the ruling could influence capex allocation toward low-carbon projects.
SHEL.L.snippet: A court ordered Shell to accelerate its emissions reduction plans in a landmark climate ruling.
SHEL.L.title: Court orders Shell to deepen emissions cuts in landmark ruling

SHEL.L.content: Shell has completed the sale of its Nigerian onshore oil and gas assets to a local consortium for $2.4 billion. The disposal ends decades of onshore operations marked by spills and theft. Shell retains its offshore and LNG interests in the country.
SHEL.L.snippet: Shell completed the sale of its Nigerian onshore assets to a local consortium.
SHEL.L.title: Shell completes sale of Nigerian onshore oil assets

SHEL.L.content: Oil prices climbed on renewed supply concerns, lifting shares across the energy sector including Shell. Brent crude added 1.8% on the day. Analysts said geopolitical risk premiums remain the key driver.
SHEL.L.snippet: Oil prices rose on supply concerns, helping lift shares of Shell and peers.
SHEL.L.title: Oil prices climb on supply concerns, lifting Shell shares

SHEL.L.content: In an interview, Shell's chief executive defended the company's dual strategy of investing in both hydrocarbons and low-carbon energy. He argued that energy security requires continued oil and gas investment. No new financial commitments were announced.
SHEL.L.snippet: Shell's chief executive discusses the balance between energy security and the low-carbon transition.
SHEL.L.title: Shell CEO interview: balancing energy security and transition

SHEL.L.content: Shell has opened one of its largest UK electric vehicle charging hubs in London, with 30 ultra-rapid chargers. The site forms part of the company's plan to expand its EV network. The investment is small relative to group capex.
SHEL.L.snippet: Shell opened one of its largest UK electric vehicle charging hubs in London.
SHEL.L.title: Shell opens major EV charging hub in London

SHEL.L.content: Analysts are split on Shell's outlook after mixed quarterly results, with bulls pointing to cash generation and bears to refining weakness. The consensus rating remains a hold. The shares yield around 4% at current prices.
SHEL.L.snippet: Brokers are divided on Shell after a mixed set of quarterly results.
SHEL.L.title: Analysts split on Shell outlook after mixed quarter

SHEL.L.content: Shell missed profit forecasts for the third quarter as weak refining margins offset steady upstream production. Adjusted earnings came in below the consensus estimate. The company kept shareholder returns unchanged, cushioning the share price reaction.
SHEL.L.snippet: Shell fell short of profit forecasts as weak refining margins offset steady production.
SHEL.L.title: Shell misses profit forecasts as refining margins weaken

ULVR.L.content: Unilever has confirmed it will spin off its ice cream division, home to Magnum and Ben & Jerry's, in a stock market listing expected to value the business at around €15 billion. The separation is the centrepiece of the CEO's plan to sharpen focus on higher-growth categories. A prospectus is expected early next year.
ULVR.L.snippet: Unilever confirmed plans to spin off its ice cream business in a listing valuing it at around €15 billion.
ULVR.L.title: Unilever to spin off ice cream business in €15bn listing

ULVR.L.content: Unilever reported third-quarter underlying sales growth ahead of expectations, with volumes returning to growth. The consumer goods giant raised its full-year underlying operating margin guidance. Management credited premiumisation and easing input cost inflation.
ULVR.L.snippet: Unilever reported better-than-expected quarterly sales and raised its margin guidance.
ULVR.L.title: Unilever Q3 sales beat expectations, raises margin guidance

ULVR.L.content: Unilever said its productivity programme will affect around 7,500 jobs globally as it seeks €800 million in cost savings. The company said most reductions would come through attrition and restructuring. Unions called for consultation on the plans.
ULVR.L.snippet: Unilever said its productivity programme would affect around 7,500 jobs globally.
ULVR.L.title: Unilever productivity programme to affect 7,500 jobs

ULVR.L.content: Unilever has completed the sale of its Russian business to a local buyer, ending a long-running exit process. The company took a modest impairment on the disposal. The business contributed a small share of group turnover.
ULVR.L.snippet: Unilever completed the sale of its Russian business to a local buyer.
ULVR.L.title: Unilever completes sale of Russian business

ULVR.L.content: Unilever confirmed its quarterly dividend, payable next month. The payout is unchanged from the prior quarter and in line with expectations. The shares yield around 3.5%.
ULVR.L.snippet: Unilever confirmed its quarterly dividend payment to shareholders.
ULVR.L.title: Unilever confirms quarterly dividend

ULVR.L.content: Unilever has launched fully recyclable packaging across its Dove range in Europe. The move is part of the company's plastic reduction commitments. The packaging change is not expected to affect pricing.
ULVR.L.snippet: Unilever launched new recyclable packaging across its Dove product range.
ULVR.L.title: Unilever launches recyclable packaging across Dove range

ULVR.L.content: A leading broker has upgraded Unilever to buy from hold, arguing that margin recovery is underappreciated. The new price target implies double-digit upside. Risks cited include volume softness in emerging markets.
ULVR.L.snippet: A leading broker upgraded Unilever to buy, citing recovering margins.
ULVR.L.title: Broker upgrades Unilever to buy on margin recovery

ULVR.L.content: Consumer goods companies including Unilever are seeing volume pressure as shoppers trade down to private-label alternatives. Industry data showed branded volumes declining for a third straight quarter. Companies are responding with promotions and pack-size adjustments.
ULVR.L.snippet: Consumer goods makers including Unilever face volume pressure as shoppers trade down.
ULVR.L.title: Consumer goods volumes under pressure as shoppers trade down

ULVR.L.content: Unilever has appointed a new chief financial officer, who will take up the role early next year. The appointee joins from another FTSE 100 company. The outgoing CFO will remain to ensure a smooth handover.
ULVR.L.snippet: Unilever named a new chief financial officer, effective early next year.
ULVR.L.title: Unilever appoints new chief financial officer

ULVR.L.content: Unilever is in focus this week ahead of its scheduled trading update on Thursday. Analysts expect modest volume growth and stable margins. The shares have outperformed the FTSE 100 this year.
ULVR.L.snippet: Unilever is in focus this week ahead of its scheduled trading update.
ULVR.L.title: FTSE 100 preview: Unilever in focus ahead of trading update
